Q: Scheme: find out if an "complex" element is in a "complex" list A:

Full implementation:

(import (scheme r5rs))
(define (is-in? e obj)
 (or
  (equal? e obj)
  (and
   (pair? obj)
   (or (is-in? e (car obj))
       (if (pair? (cdr obj))
        (let contain-e?
             [[tocheck (cdr obj)]]
         (or
          (is-in? e (car tocheck)) 
          (let [[rest (cdr tocheck)]]
           (if (pair? rest)
            (contain-e? rest)
            (and (not (null? e)) (equal? e rest))))))
        (and (not (null? e)) (equal? e (cdr obj))))))))

This works on all 11 examples given and is easy to read. Enjoy.

P.S.: I thought of some other conditions you didn't mention:

(is-in? 3 '(1 2 . 3)) ;-> #t
(is-in? '() (1 2)) ; -> #f
(is-in? '() '(1 2 ())) ; -> #t

Change (if (pair a) b (and (not (null? e)) _)) into (and (pair a) b) if you want them all to be #false.

Q: Refresh disabled in copied PowerQuery A:

The reason your Refresh button is disabled is likely because you Copied and Pasted the table cells rather than the query connection itself. This often creates a static snapshot instead of a linked Power Query table.

You can fix it by using a Query connection

Follow the below given method & steps:

The Duplication Method

Instead of copying cells, duplicate the query logic so both remain linked to the source.
Steps: -

  • Open the Queries & Connections pane (Data tab).

  • Right-click your original query and select Duplicate.

  • A new query will open. Click Close & Load To... and select the new worksheet.

  • Add your 'Amount' slicer to this new table.

Q: Snowflake count_if returns 0 if no records satisfy the condition, while the documentation states otherwise A:

In Snowflake, COUNT_IF returns 0 when no rows satisfy the condition because it counts the number of rows where the condition is TRUE. If there are rows but none meet the condition, the result is 0; it only returns NULL when there are no input rows at all (e.g., after filtering).

Q: azure web app maximum request length exceeded A:

If you have setup your web application under Azure Web Application Firewall gateway, you should be able to increase or specify the upload limit by following the below steps.

The file upload limit field is specified in MB and it governs the maximum allowed file upload size. This field can have a minimum value of 1 MB and a maximum of 500 MB for Large SKU instances while Medium SKU has a maximum of 100 MB. The default value for file upload limit is 100 MB.

But if you have not setup under Azure Application Gateway Web Application Firewall, then this solution might not be helpful for you.

You can also refer to the below document for more info : https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/application-gateway-waf-configuration

Q: UIAutomation: AddAutomationEventHandler() returns E_POINTER A:

Okay, it feels like some WinAPI related code, since I was able to found link to winapi.

AutomationElementMode_None tells UI Automation to fetch the requested properties and disconnect the COM object from the underlying UI target to improve performance. The resulting sender object in your callback is essentially a read-only data snapshot. It contains the cached properties (which is why get_CachedControlType works), but it holds no reference to the actual live window or control.

So, I would suggest basically without having the actual working MRE just try to replace it with AutomationElementMode_Full so you would have an actual object and be able to resolve the problem in the code above.
